newsitem.title: USA: Mass Weld to focus on construction jobs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mass Weld to focus on construction jobs - paper.

text.p: Massachusetts Gov. William Weld, one day after losing a senate race to U.S. Senator John Kerry, said he was switching his focus to jump-starting construction jobs, the Boston Globe said on Thursday.

"I intend to be a sensational Gov. Pothole," Weld told the paper, in an interview. This was a twist on a reference to U.S. Senator Al D'Amato, R-N.Y., who has built a strong political base by serving local constituents.

Legislative leaders have warned that the state's $900 million construction budget already is stretched to the limit, but Weld said that if he uses up the capital budget, he might tap the state's $17 billion operating budget, the Globe said.
And he hinted that if the state runs another surplus, he might spend the money instead of returning it to taxpayers.
Weld's new stance marks a sharp reversal from his previous emphasis on fiscal conservatism, fighting crime and reducing welfare and taxes, the paper said.
The paper listed the following projects as ones Weld hopes to get going.

--A 600,000 square-foot convention center in Boston, whose overall price tag could run as high as $500 million. Weld said it would attract eight new hotels and revitalize the area. A commission is studying the project and no bill has been filed.
--A big expansion of Worcester's convention center. The legislature agreed to supply $17 million. The bill stalled this summer, though legislative leaders want to try again soon.
--A big expansion of the Basketball Hall of Fame in Springfield. The bill for Worcester's new funds included $25 million for this project and legislative leaders hope for quick action.

--Attracting a minor league baseball team to Springfield, which has identified a site and needs $14 million from the state to help build a stadium. No bill has been filed, and the House Speaker has said he does not like the idea of spending public money on privately owned sports franchises.

--A sports complex in Lowell, for which the legislature has agreed to fund an $8 million stadium and a $14 million hockey arena for the University of Massachusetts at Lowell. Minor-league teams are also expected to rent the complex.

--A 300,000 square-foot aquarium and marine science center in New Bedford. The state has spent $300,000 on a feasibility study and would need to spend another $1 million. No bill has been filed and the House Speaker is skeptical, saying similar projects around the country have lost money.

--Revitalizing the Fore River Shipyard. the state agreed to sell the yard to a shipbuilder for $20 million less than it paid for it, and to spend $3 million cleaning it up. Weld wants another $10 million state commitment to lay the groundwork for hundreds of millions of dollars of federal loan guarantees. No bill has been filed.

--Renovating Battleship Cove in Fall River. Weld wants to spend $10 million on the project, and while the legislature has provided some, the rest of the funds are stalled along with those for Worcester and Springfield.
